explanation: Drawn around 1490, it tests a claim by the Roman architect Vitruvius that a well-proportioned human body fits inside both shapes. It is named after him.

claims.text: Leonardo da Vinci's Vitruvian Man shows a man with outstretched arms and legs inscribed in a circle and a square.
Vitruvian Man does not show a triangle, a hexagon or a star around the figure.
Vitruvius, a Roman architect, wrote that a well-proportioned human body can be fitted into both a circle and a square.
The drawing Vitruvian Man is named after Vitruvius.
